overlap_rationale: Both articles are single-authored ethnographies by Nikhil Anand (supported by the same SSRC, Wenner-Gren, and NSF grants) drawing on the same overarching ~2-year ("nearly two years" / "22 months") ethnographic fieldwork conducted in Mumbai between 2007 and 2010 on the Mumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) water supply system in northern Mumbai. Part of the underlying fieldwork sample and institutional data is shared: both papers draw on interviews and ethnographic observations with BMC ward and city water engineers during 2007–2008 and report shared institutional findings regarding Mumbai's pre-1995 residency cutoff rule for slum water eligibility, non-functioning water meters (over half not working, leading to estimated bills), and municipal engineers' discretionary handling of unauthorized connections and leaks. However, each article analyzes a substantially distinct actor subset, focal site, and empirical case within that multi-site fieldwork without any overlapping named/pseudonymous informants or vignettes: Study A examines the 2004–2007 World Bank/Castalia Water Distribution Improvement Project (WDIP) water audit controversy in K-East ward through consultant interviews (Haresh), senior BMC planning engineers, and field visits with ward engineer Patankar, whereas Study B examines municipal disconnection and infrastructural abjection in the Muslim settlement of Premnagar (Jogeshwari) through interviews and observations with Muslim settlers (Asif, Salim, Abdul), plumbers (Rafiq-bhai, Ahmed), and BMC engineers (Rané, Gupte). Because both draw on the same 2007–2010 BMC fieldwork in northern Mumbai with overlapping municipal-utility/engineer ethnography alongside distinct community vs consultancy sub-samples, this pair represents partial sample overlap with moderate synthesis double-counting risk if city/utility-level findings on legal cutoffs, metering, and informal connections are pooled as independent studies.
study_a_sample_and_data: Ethnographic and documentary study in Mumbai, India, focusing on K-East ward (Andheri East, population ~806,360) and the Mumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) Hydraulic Engineering Department. Draws on nearly two years of ethnographic fieldwork (specific vignettes dated June–December 2007 and February 2008) plus audit documents from the 2004–2007 World Bank-funded Water Distribution Improvement Project (WDIP) conducted by Castalia Strategic Advisors. No fixed quantitative N; qualitative sample comprises World Bank management consultants (e.g., Haresh), senior BMC water engineers, and field shadowing of ward water engineer Patankar and maintenance crews/councilors.
study_b_sample_and_data: Ethnographic study in Premnagar ('Squatters Colony'), a predominantly Muslim settlement (>40,000 registered adult voters) in Jogeshwari, northern Mumbai, India, and the local BMC ward water office. Based on 22 months of fieldwork conducted between 2007 and 2010 (specific vignettes dated late 2007 to December 2008). No fixed quantitative N; qualitative sample comprises Muslim settlers/households in Premnagar (e.g., Asif, Salim, Abdul, women's savings group), local plumbers mediating legal and unauthorized connections (e.g., Rafiq-bhai, Ahmed), and BMC ward/city water engineers (e.g., Rané, Gupte, Assistant Engineer).
